newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Christopher will go to Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Christopher will go to Mideast.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher will go to the Middle East this weekend for the start of talks between Israel and the Palestinians on a variety of issues left unsettled at this week's Middle East summit, President Bill Clinton said on Friday.

"We discussed it and I think he probably has finalised his plans by now. I told him I wanted him to go there for the start of the talks," Clinton told reporters outside a New York State hotel where is preparing for Sunday's presidential campaign debate with Republican rival Bob Dole.

Clinton said Christopher, who State Department sources said would meet separately with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, would then go on to a planned visit to sub-Saharan Africa.

Israeli and Palestinian officials will meet on Sunday at Erez, on the border between Israel and Gaza, to discuss implementation of their peace accords, including an Israeli troop deployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Washington has already announced that Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will attend the talks, organized in the wake of bloody Israeli-Palestinian clashes last week.
The State Department sources said in Washington it was unclear whether Christopher would attend those talks, which Netanyahu and Arafat themselves are not scheduled to attend.
